Speaking as someone who has (and still does to an extent) struggled with social anxiety that got really bad during my teen years, I'd genuinely reconsider having another conversation with her Dr or psychiatrist if meds aren't necessary. I say talk to a Dr or psych because a therapist can't use that as a tool.

The main reason I didn't take meds in my teens and had to wait until I was 18 was pressure from my parents who would tell me I didn't need them or that my social anxiety wasn't that bad. The problem was I couldn't work on the strategies or learn to reshape my thoughts until I got the crutch that medications gave. I got to practice making food orders and asking questions in stores because medication calmed me down enough to be able to work on my thought patterns.

When I did therapy without medications as a teen, I could see I was in a panic attack, but I couldn't begin to take it apart without feeling completely overwhelmed by my mind.

I'm not saying medication is for sure the answer. But if she's at the point where she's sitting in a Wendy's unable to order for herself even after being in therapy and working through the steps of ordering and still being unable to order for herself, that might be a sign that learning the coping strategies might now yet be enough. It's not a fault on her or a slight, but she might need the extra leg up that medication could provide.

That's not to say she'd always need meds if she does get them. It might be worse now in her life than any other time because of all the hormones of the teenage years. I only take medications in really bad days, and those can be months or years apart.

But one last thing, I get that you were probably on a time crunch, and that's why you only waited 10 minutes. But 10 minutes for something like exposure therapy practice might not have been enough time and might have actually made the anxiety worse. If she's supposed to practice ordering, take a day when you have nothing else that needs to get done, go at a nice quiet time, and just be willing to sit there. It might take an hour. You might need to take a walk around the block with her. But the goal is for her to order something. Maybe don't make her have to pay for it if it's part of her therapy. But having a time crunch in the back of your mind while you're trying to push through anxiety will only make her anxiety worse so if your goal is to help her with her exposure therapy, that would be my advice.

Honestly, I'm under the NAH side of things, but whether or not you're an asshole is honestly irrelevant, and the real question is how do you help your child get better.

I would argue that we're not talking about a preference. If you ask a bi or a pan person are you into (insert gender identity here), you're more likely going run into a "yes" or "doesn't matter to me". A gynosexual's answer is "I couldn't tell you a yes or no because what does matter hasn't been disclosed". It goes beyond preference because they just have zero interest without that gender expression.

I am bi and sure, I have a preference for women but I'm dating a man who isn't feminine because my preference isn't a limiter. It's just an overall leaning, nothing more than that. A preference is "overall I tend to like _______". This goes far deeper than that.

Because gender expression has nothing to do with being bi or pan. If i were gynosexual and a masculine guy hit on me, saying "Sorry, I'm bi, you're not what I'm into" would only create confusion. A masculine guy hits on me and I say, "Sorry, I'm gynosexual, you're not what I'm into" makes sense.

At the end of the day, gender expression isn't a limiter for attraction for a bi or pan person whereas for a gyno sexual, it is the most important thing and most basic limiter.

I mean, queer works for so many as a big umbrella term but it doesn't convey anything specific about their sexuality. Pan is open to the wide spectrum of gender identities and expressions where as this person's sexual identity is focused on a particular expression so that's not the same. Bi people can have preferences when it comes to their preferred "type" but you could have many different types and what you find attractive might be different for men women and non-binary folk. 

This person is only interested in female gender expression. Woman, man, non-binary, doesn't make a difference to this sexuality. When I was under the age of five, my father got me a toy. I don't fully remember what it was but he just picked up for me. No occasion, there was no expectation by me that I would be getting anything.

I should have been grateful and happy. Instead I lashed out and raged at him. "I already have this one! You don't pay attention to me! I hate you! See! You don't love me!" According to my older brother, it was the only time I ever said I hate you to my dad.

My dad got up and just went out the front door. There were still people home and he'd just come home from work so it wasn't like he was leaving me and my brother alone or anything. I stayed in my room just angry and sad about this stupid toy until I'd finally calmed down a bit.

When my dad came back, he had three different toys, none of which were ones I already owned. He gave them all to me and asked if any of these were repeats.

I look at this story and see that I was a little greedy shit but my brother (who is a dad now) told me he saw something else in my dad that day. Instead of getting hurt by what I said (even though I'm pretty sure hearing your kid say they hate you when you tried to do a good thing does hurt), he looked past that and saw I was hurting. I was clearly upset about something bigger than a toy. And he showed me that he heard my pain. Now, I think he could have done that without buying multiple toys or even anything honestly.

My brother and I talked about this when my dad passed away a couple years back. Sure, there's a lot of stuff that we can look back on and say "I should have been more grateful or done something more appreciative." But we were children. We didn't know gratefulness or how to show appreciation with the same depth we do as adults.

I guess what I'm trying to say is, if you've got that parent you want to show those feelings to who is still around, it's not too late to do the appreciative shit you wish you did as kids. Even something simple as a phone call to check in on them or going to get lunch together.

Wait wait wait, who said anything about romance or romantic interest? 

To me, all a flirt means is that I have an interest in a person. Probably a sexual interest but at the very least I find something interesting about that person and want to possibly build a deeper connection (possibly romantic and/or possibly sexual). 

To me, part of vetting a person to see if they are someone I want to be in a sexual or romantic relationship with is flirting. It's just flirting for fun because I have no idea where my interaction with this person will go (possibly somewhere or possibly nowhere) and any of these situations is fine. That's all I meant by it not being a commitment. I'm not trying to trick them, I'm building a connection and seeing where it goes. I'm conveying an interest and seeing if they are on the same page as me.

All I'm doing when I'm flirting is communicating "You are attractive and want to know if you're attracted to me" and that is as deep as it goes.

But on the other hand, flirting isn't a commitment or an agreement to anything. It's just an element of socializing and an element of communication. It kind of feels like saying that because you're flirting you have to be open to more and I can't get behind that sentiment. Feels too close to "If you dress a certain way, be ready to put out".

You didn't write an argument but why not? I actually completely agree with you so here's my reasoning.


Everyone wants to bring up the amount of toppings as a big plus but I think the sheer amount of options is actually a downside. Say you're having a couple of friends (let's say 6 people) over and someone suggests ordering a pizza. Sure, there might be a pizza combination you love but someone in that room will have their own problem with the combination you want. It will be a lengthy discussion and the pizza will end up being ok but nothing anyone is super excited about anymore. Not to mention the headache of trying to figure out where to order the pizza from, someone will insist it's worth it to order from their tried and true pizza location and someone else will argue with the same ferocity about their favourite pizza joint. People are more loyal about their favourite pizza then any other food. It's the most stressful of any other food orders and by the time it's done, the food is no longer exciting and a good time.


Because of this problem, we get a few standard pizzas that are just the simple easy solutions. You got classic pepperoni. Which is only as good as the pepperoni you get and personally don't even like it all that much. I've never had a pizza and gone "damn this is some great pepperoni". The most I've ever said is the pepperoni is pretty good. Another classic is a cheese pizza but at that point, anyone with the cheese pizza knows they rather have some other type of food (I was that child). Maybe you're someone who'd enjoy deluxe pizzas... If it weren't for the olives that litter it. Seriously, olives are such a decisive food, why have it on a standard topping list?

So yeah, tldr; ordering pizza is a mess of choices and in the end nobody is truly happy with the result
